facts.name: Eastern Blue Star
facts.color: Pale blue star-shaped flowers; golden fall leaves
facts.light: Full sun to part shade; blooms best in sun and may flop in deep shade
facts.moisture: Average to moist; drought tolerant once established
facts.notes: A long-lived clump of willow-like leaves topped with clusters of pale blue star flowers in late spring, then golden-yellow fall color. Deer usually leave it alone because of its milky sap. Native to the eastern and central U.S., but not to Michigan.
facts.toxSrc: Its milky latex sap is toxic (UW–Madison Extension); not on the ASPCA list

sources.title: English Gardens (Michigan garden center): Blue Ice Star Flower
sources.note: A Michigan garden center sells the 'Blue Ice' variety of this plant. Not native to Michigan (Wildflower Center range), so listed as a garden favorite.

sources.title: MSU Horticulture Gardens: Perennial inventory, spring plant sale 2021
sources.note: Michigan State's plant sale lists the 'Storm Cloud' variety: zones 4 to 9, full to part sun, late spring to early summer, 24 to 30 in tall.

sources.title: Wisconsin Horticulture (UW–Madison Extension): Willowleaf bluestar
sources.note: 2 to 3 ft tall and wide; pale blue flowers mid-spring into early summer; sun to light shade; moist loam but adapts, drought tolerant once established; zones 3a to 9b; golden fall color; deer avoid it (latex). Deadhead or cut back by a third to a half after flowering; rarely needs dividing. Leaves and stems exude a toxic white latex.

sources.title: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center: Amsonia tabernaemontana
sources.note: Native from Maryland and Virginia to southern Illinois, Kansas, Florida and Texas; Michigan is not in its native range.

sources.title: Chicago Botanic Garden: Amsonia tabernaemontana
sources.note: Blooms May to June; full sun or part shade; zones 3 to 9; golden-yellow fall color; deer resistant.

sources.title: Perennials.com (Walters Gardens): Amsonia tabernaemontana
sources.note: 23 to 35 in tall, 29 to 35 in wide; light blue flowers late spring and early summer; zones 3 to 9; deer resistant.

companions.why: Try combining it with Siberian iris, butterfly weed, daylilies and dark-colored heucheras; in woodland gardens it goes with ferns, bleeding heart and sedges.
